text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Opposition centrist Union for Freedom leader Leszek Balcerowicz said the governing leftist coalition acts against Poland's municipalities and makes them ever more dependent on central government subsidies.

- By 2015 the number of Poles with higher education must reach levels reflecting the EU average for the country to become the Union's worthy partner. The Education Ministry has laid out a programme for educational system reform to lead to an increase in the number of university students.
- Pork prices in the first half of 1997 will range from four to 4.2 zlotys per kilogramme, the Agricultural Market Agency (ARR), the government market regulator, said.
- The parliamentary committee for coal mining restructuring wants the government to produce a sector development strategy for the period up to 2010.
The present development programme does not contain long-term investment decisions, committee members said.

- Poland's Non-Ferrous Metals Economic Chamber, which groups metal producers, has protested against envisaged liberalisation in non-ferrous metals trading, saying it would lead to production cost growth.
The metal traders argued that the ban on imports would hurt the customer since the metal produced abroad is cheaper than that made in Poland.
- TPSA, Poland's telecommunications monopolist, will invest 6.4 million zlotys in billing equipment in the Warsaw province this year, TPSA representatives said.
- Coca Cola Poland will invest $100 million in production development in the coming twelve months.
"Poland's market is ready for doubling Coca Cola beverage consumption", the concern's director general Douglas Ivester said.
NOWA EUROPA
- The Danish Danfoss company has purchased a department in the Wroclaw-based Agromet Pilamet agricultural machinery plant for 11 million marks.
Danfoss will invest up to 10 million marks in the department's modernisation, the contract says.
- Poland's Insurance Chamber (PIU) is developing a ranking of insurance firms which will help the customer to choose the best offer.
- Sopot-based Hestia Insurace company management and the firm's Alte Lepziger major shareholder said that no conflict has taken place in the company, proving wrong a previous report in Nowa Europa.
- TPSA, the telecoms monopolist, has threatened Polkomtel SA, the digital GSM mobile phone operator, that it will cut system connections if Polkomtel does not accept TPSA service pricing conditions.
Polkomtel has temporarily accepted the terms so as not to hurt its customers but intends to renegotiate the deal.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Over 100 producers of musical instruments, sound systems and special effects equipment will exhibit their products at the Music Expo Intermedia international fair in Wroclaw in mid-October.
- The Czech Motor Zetor tractor maker will introduce its new Indian-made 19 KW agricultural tractor on the Polish market. Tractor sales will start in 1997 and the price will not exceed 22,000 zlotys.
- Poland's housing construction declined by 15.5 percent this August compared with the results in the same period last year, according to the Central Statistics Office (GUS).
- International supermarket chains operating in Poland are demanding extra charges from local producers and suppliers to cover the promotion costs of their products, the chains' representaives say.
ZYCIE WARSZAWY
- The police have arrested bootleggers who smuggled 240,000 litres of rectified spirit into Poland in the Lodz province, central Poland.

- Poland's co-ruling Polish Peasants Party (PSL) Leszno province regional caucus has called for the support of Roman Jagielinski as the future party leader in the coming PSL congress to elect the party leadership.
